newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - June 27.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- FINANCE DIRECTOR QUITS GRAND MET

Gerald Corbett, finance director of Grand Metropolitan who lost out on the job of finance director of the planned merged group GMG Brands, has resigned. The move comes six months earlier than GrandMet had said when it announced the proposed merger with Guinness on May 12. A statement from the company said the departure had been mutually agreed.
-- EMAP'S 120 PER CENT BONUS SCHEME

Media group Emap has altered a long-term bonus scheme so that it now allows for bonuses worth up to 120 per cent of directors' basic salaries. The move was disclosed in the annual report of the magazines and radio group, published on Thursday. The report also reveals that Emap paid 1.11 million stg in compensation to former directors.
-- FLEXTECH HOLDERS CUT THEIR STAKES

Pearson, the media and leisure group, and the BBC have both sold large parts of their stakes in Flextech, the cable TV group. Pearson sold four million shares, raising 24 million stg, in a move which leaves it with 4.8 million remaining shares -- three per cent of the company. The BBC sold 3.8 million shares, amounting to over two-thirds of its stake in the group. Both Pearson and the BBC have agreed not to sell their remaining holdings until next April.
THE TIMES
-- BONN TO SELL 10 BILLION STG TELEKOM STAKE

The German government is planning to sell a 10 billion stg stake in Deutsche Telekom, the partially privatised national telecoms operator. The move is part of attempts by Bonn to reduce its budget deficit in order to qualify for European monetary union. Under the plans, which will be scrutinised by Eurostat, the government will transfer a 25 per cent Telekom share package worth 10 billion stg to the state development agency.
-- NORMAN TAKES PAY CUT AT ASDA

Archie Norman, the high-profile chief executive of supermarket chain Asda ASDD.L, is to take a pay cut at the group after being appointed vice-chairman of the Conservative Party. Norman, who received 3.69 million stg from Asda in 1995-96, was elected as a Conservative MP in May. He has said he intends to stay with the company "to see it through the next phase" and will spend one or two days a week on his Asda duties.
-- POULENC TO AIM FOR FFr25 BILLION RORER DEAL

Rhone-Poulenc, the French chemicals, polymers and pharmaceuticals group, is planning to spend FFr25 billion to take full control of its U.S.-listed drugs company as part of a strategy to concentrate on pharmaceuticals. Shares in the drugs group, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer (RPR), rose on the news.
Rhone-Poulenc already holds a 68.3 per cent stake in RPR, which owns the UK- based drugs company Fisons and the vaccines company Pasteur Merieux Connaught.
THE GUARDIAN
-- DRINKS TRIO IN SECRET TALKS

Behind-the-scenes attempts are being made to remove the obstacle posed by French luxury goods group LVMH to the proposed mega-merger between drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan. Secret overtures are being made which could lead to talks on a possible three-way merger involving the groups.
LVMH, which holds a 14.3 per cent stake in Guinness, has spent over 810 million stg acquiring a 6.3 per cent holding in GrandMet as part of its attempt to block the merger.
-- MILTON KEYNES RACKS UP TITLE AS TOP MALL

A survey of Britain's 900 shopping centres has judged that Milton Keynes has the best shops, the best environment and the best facilities. The study was undertaken by consultancy Retail Directions, which ranked Milton Keynes ahead of better-known retail destinations such as Lakeside at Thurrock, Merry Hill in Dudley and the MetroCentre at Gateshead.
-- DEMI MOORE CREATES A FIZZ

Pepsi, the U.S. soft drinks giant, is to take on the French companies Perrier and Evian in the U.S. market for bottled water. While Perrier dominates the U.S. market, Evian is famous as the water of choice of actress Demi Moore when shampooing her hair on the set. Pepsi has launched a ferocious marketing campaign for its Aquafina brand of still water. The market for bottled water in the U.S. is growing at eight per cent this year, while sales of water in smaller bottles are growing at 30 per cent.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- GUS PLAN TO END CATALOGUE OF WOES

In an attempt to boost its sagging home shopping division, catalogue retailer Great Universal Stores has planned an attack on the direct sales market, which includes plans to distribute four new catalogues to customers' homes. GUS chairman Lord Wolfson has also revealed plans to offer GUS customers personal loans and insurance products to increase the size of the GUS financial division.
-- GATES IN THE WAY WHEN ELLISON CONSULTS ORACLE

The battle between Oracle and Microsoft has heated up once again with Oracle chairman Larry Ellison accusing Bill Gates of stealing his thunder with his pledge to donate $200m to equip schools and libraries with personal computers. Ellison doubts that it is a coincidence Gates's announcement arrived 24 hours before a pledge of his own to spend $100 million to help put Network Computers on the desks of pupils across the U.S.
-- ASDA PUTS PRESSURE ON RIVALS AS FOOD SALES SOAR

Supermarket chain Asda has revealed that its sales are growing at twice the average rate in the UK food sales sector. Asda is the latest of the 'big four' UK supermarket chains to announce a rise in market share, a trend which has raised concerns that second-tier players such as Kwik-Save and Somerfield are being squeezed out. Like-for-like sales at Asda grew at 9.2 per cent in the year to the end of May, compared to 7.5 per cent at Tesco.
